releases.name: v0.68.0: Hands Off Their Children
releases.body:
### Added

- **A step that starts after the interrupt is logged** ([#14](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/14)). A request that ends with tool calls interrupts its session so the runner does not start another step, and that interrupt is fire-and-forget: the runner can begin the next step before the host handles it. The stray step is wasted (extra tokens, a stray assistant message in history) but never wrong for the caller, so it is counted rather than prevented. At `logLevel: debug`, every step the host starts after plugboard asked for an interrupt writes `request.stray_step` with the step count, how many were stray and whether the response had already finished. A run of real traffic then says whether the race can be ignored or needs the upstream change (#3's native backend has no loop to race).

### Changed

- **`tool_choice` is documented as a request, not a guarantee** ([#13](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/13)). The OpenCode session API has no tool-choice control, so `required` and a named function reach the model as a system instruction plus a narrowed tool list, and a model can answer in text instead. That was true and undocumented on the front page. The README now says so, next to what the APIs serve, and a test pins the documented result: a scripted model that ignores the instruction gets its text answer back as a normal 200, with no `tool_calls` and no error. The alternative, answering 400 when a request needs a guarantee plugboard cannot give, was rejected: it would break the pydantic-ai and `with_structured_output` callers that were checked and work today, for a risk that has not been seen.

### Fixed

- **A host change that breaks tool renaming fails the request instead of sending no tools** ([#199](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/199)). Plugboard offers a caller's tools by renaming its placeholder seeds in the `context` hook, and the host finds them again by the identity of the descriptor object, a rule it states only in a comment. If a host upgrade handed out copies, froze the descriptors or matched by key alone, every renamed tool would be dropped without an error and the model would answer with no tools at all, while `tsc` stayed green because no type changed. The hook now checks its own output: every tool it leaves in place must be a descriptor object the host handed it, or the request fails with the usual 500 `backend_preparation_failed` and a `request.seed_rename_failed` log line naming the tools. A request that used to fail silently now fails visibly.
- **Pruning gives up a request session that has a child session instead of deleting it** (found in review of the abandoned #200 change). OpenCode deletes a session's children when the session is deleted, so the sweep's removal could take a session plugboard never created: a session started under the request, or another plugin's child. A fork is not at risk: it is stored as a top-level session, not a child, and it is never in the index. A request session allows no tool that could start a child, so any child there is someone else's. On OpenCode 2.1 and later the sweep now asks the host for the session's children and, when there are any, gives the request up: the index entry is dropped and the session is never deleted, even after those children are removed. Once pruning finds children, plugboard relinquishes the request permanently, and it stops counting toward `maxSessions` and `maxAgeDays`. On 2.0.x, whose plugin API cannot list sessions, the removal goes ahead without that protection and can delete the children too. The check is made just before the delete, so a child created in between is still taken with the session: OpenCode has no conditional delete. The sweep line gains a `relinquished` count, and the runtime version is 18, so a server that hot-reloads the plugin needs a restart.
- **The manual cleanup tool deletes only what it can prove.** `examples/_tools/sessions.py` matched sessions on

releases.name: v0.67.0: Runs on OpenCode 2.4
releases.body:
### Changed

- **Runs on OpenCode 2.4** ([#703](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/pull/703)). The host peer range is now `>=2.0.26 <2.5` and the dev pin is 2.4.2, which CI's host matrix now tests. OpenCode 2.4.2 shipped on 2026-11-26, and a host that respects the peer range had skipped it every hour since: aihub's autoupdate logged "skip 2.4.2: outside opencode-plugboard@0.66.0 peer range >=2.0.26 <2.4". The daily host bump only covers versions inside the range, so this one was run by hand with the same script.
- **A tool's `codemode` option may be an object.** OpenCode 2.4 widened it from `boolean` to `boolean | { pinned, description, input, output }`, and `isDirect` in `src/session/host.ts`, which decides what `opencodeTools` offers a caller, accepted only the boolean. The type check failed at both `ctx.tool.list()` filters, and it would fail for anyone who typechecks the shipped source as well. `isDirect` now takes the host's own listed-tool type, so the next shape change fails there instead of being read as "not direct". Behaviour is unchanged: a tool is direct only when `codemode` is `false`, and the object form is Code Mode. `effect` is still 4.1.0, and nothing else in the API the plugin uses changed shape.

## The full story

13 commits since v0.66.0, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Docs (2)</summary>

**docs(changelog): notes for 0.67.0, OpenCode 2.4 support** ([`ba95c88`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/ba95c88f49ddc29b5f7024ad4425472860307332))

The release script refuses an empty [Unreleased], so this fills it for 0.67.0 from #703: the peer range widening to <2.5 with the dev pin at 2.4.2, and the codemode type change that came with it.

The second bullet is written for the reader who typechecks the shipped source, because that is who the break hit: OpenCode 2.4 widened a tool's `codemode` option to an object, and the old narrow parameter in `isDirect` failed compilation instead of a runtime check. It says plainly that behaviour is unchanged, so nobody reads it as a fix to a tool-listing bug.

Checked: `bun .github/scripts/since-next.ts --check` reports no placeholder in a released section.

**docs(releasing): the release script bumps install pins** ([`467fc5b`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/467fc5b6433543538b0c330af5097e37b54ff7ac))

docs/releasing.md said to update `opencode-plugboard@x.y.z` in README.md and docs/clients/any-app.md by hand because the release script did not touch them. The script now imports `bumpInstallPins` and rewrites the pin in README.md and every docs/**/*.md, which `bun run release 0.67.0 --dry-run` confirms. The step now says so.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Dependencies (11)</summary>

**build(deps): support opencode 2.4.2** ([`284744e`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/284744ef3c428471d25889cd6500198357869221))

OpenCode 2.4.2 shipped on 2026-11-26, but the plugboard peer range stopped at <2.4, so hosts that respect it still skip it (aihub's autoupdate logs "skip 2.4.2: outside opencode-plugboard@0.66.0 peer range >=2.0.26 <2.4" every hour). The daily host bump only covers versions inside the range, so this one was run by hand with the same script: `bun .github/scripts/host-bump.ts 2.4.2`.

- devDependency @opencode/plugin 2.3.2 -> 2.4.2 (effect stays 4.1.0, the version 2.4.2 pins)
- peer @opencode/plugin >=2.0.26 <2.4 -> >=2.0.26 <2.5
- npm-shrinkwrap.json regenerated per docs/packaging.md, so its root peer range matches package.json

OpenCode 2.4 widened a tool's `Options.codemode` from `boolean` to `boolean | { pinned, description, input, output }` and added CMInput and CMOutput to `Tool.Info`. `isDirect` in src/session/host.ts accepted only `codemode?: boolean`, so both `ctx.tool.list()` filters failed the typecheck. It now takes `ListedTool`, derived from the host's own `ctx.tool.list()` return type, so the next shape change fails

releases.name: v0.66.0: OpenCode 2.3 support
releases.body:
### Changed

- **Runs on OpenCode 2.3** ([#700](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/pull/700)). The host peer range is now `>=2.0.26 <2.4` and the dev pin is 2.3.2, which CI's host matrix now tests. Hosts that respect the peer range stayed on 2.2.7 until now: aihub's autoupdate skipped 2.3.2 every hour from 2026-11-18. The daily host bump only handles versions inside the range, so this one was run by hand with the same script. It replaces dependabot's #699, which failed every job on a frozen lockfile.
- **Dependencies.** About 25 routine bumps covering GitHub Actions and the example apps. No runtime behaviour change.

### Fixed

- **Release script takes the previous version from tags that exist** ([7b066e1](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/7b066e1)).

## The full story

28 commits since v0.65.2, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Fixes (1)</summary>

**fix(release): take the previous version from tags that exist** ([`7b066e1`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/7b066e142448f8b08cfb81eb7470551afa15b68f))

release.ts read the previous version from the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] compare link, and release-notes.ts from the next heading down. A release that failed after its commit reached main (0.65.0 CI, 0.65.1 Publish) left a heading and link for a tag that never existed. The next release then failed on git log v0.65.0..HEAD, and Publish failed with "tag v0.65.0 is not in this clone". Recovery needed a hand-edited link (#653) and an extra patch release (0.65.2).

release.ts now uses the linked version only when its tag exists, else the newest v* tag below the new version. release-notes.ts walks the headings below the section to the first with a tag. Rejected: a CHANGELOG-only fix, which leaves the next failed release to break the same way.

Validation: release-notes.ts 0.65.1 now gives "Full diff v0.64.0...v0.65.1" (it exited 1 before). release.ts --dry-run with the link set to nonexistent v0.65.9 resolves the previous version to 0.65.2. bun run typecheck passes.

Closes #657

</details>

<details>
<summary>Docs (1)</summary>

**docs(changelog): notes for 0.66.0, OpenCode 2.3 support** ([`dfab82d`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/dfab82d807781adf79346df24c787d2708a00d64))

Curated [Unreleased] entry so the release script has something to ship: the peer range widening from #700, the routine bumps, and the release-script tag fix.

</details>

releases.name: v0.65.2: Third Time Lucky
releases.body:
### Changed

- **Runs on OpenCode 2.2.7** ([#646](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/pull/646)). The host peer range is now `>=2.0.26 <2.3`, and the optional `effect` peer accepts 4.1.0. This closes the 2.2.6 and 2.2.7 load-check failures ([#622](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/622), [#647](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/647)).
- **Dependencies.** About 40 routine bumps merged, covering the `ai` SDK, `@opentui/core`, `conventional-commits-parser`, `fast-xml-parser`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, GitHub Actions, and the example apps. No runtime behaviour change.

### Fixed

- **Anthropic usage speed for SDK 1.3.** The Messages response carries the usage `speed` field the 1.3 SDK requires ([ddc8245](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/ddc8245)).
- **The 0.65.0 and 0.65.1 releases never reached npm.** 0.65.0 was not tagged: its merge CI failed on a racing test, fixed in [#651](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/pull/651). 0.65.1 was tagged, but its Publish run failed at "Build the release notes" because the changelog's previous heading (0.65.0) had no tag, so npm kept 0.64.0. This patch carries their changes. Its release notes now find the previous tag, v0.65.1.

## The full story

1 commit since v0.65.1, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Docs (1)</summary>

**docs(changelog): write the 0.65.2 notes; 0.65.0 and 0.65.1 never reached npm** ([`8898883`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/8898883f47614c85bb242818219f0908c335b4ba))

0.65.0 was not tagged (merge CI failed on a racing test, fixed in #651). 0.65.1 was tagged, but its Publish run failed at "Build the release notes": the changelog heading below it is 0.65.0, and v0.65.0 does not exist. Tags cannot move, so the fix goes forward as 0.65.2. Its previous heading is 0.65.1, whose tag exists, so the notes step can run.

Validation: git diff origin/main shows only CHANGELOG.md and README.md.

</details>

---

**Full diff:** [v0.65.1...v0.65.2](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/compare/v0.65.1...v0.65.2)

releases.name: v0.64.0: Every Request, Kept
releases.body:
### Added

- **Every model request is stored whole, by default** ([#586](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/586)). Each authenticated model request, on every API, leaves one record under its app: the request as received (method, path, query, every header, the body byte for byte), the response as sent (status, headers, the full body, a stream's raw SSE bytes), the timing, the routing (model requested and served, the fallback chain, breaker decisions, cache result), the usage and cost, the model's full answer assembled from the stream, and every error with its full body, the host's own error included. An app's key reads its own record with `GET /plugboard/requests/{request id or session id}`; another app's id is a 404. Only the values of `Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `x-goog-api-key` and a `key` query parameter are redacted. The option is `history.storeRequestBody` (default `true`, per app under `apps.<name>.history`); `false` stores nothing. Nothing is capped or pruned, and images and streams can be megabytes per request. The option name `history` was a retired spelling of `sessions`; its old fields now say they moved there.
- **The request log line shows how big the request was** ([#586](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/issues/586)). Each model request logs `body_bytes`, and the count and bytes of its system prompts, messages and tools (`system_count`, `system_bytes`, `message_count`, `message_bytes`, `tool_count`, `tool_bytes`). A small question that costs thousands of cached prompt tokens now shows where they come from, usually the tool list.

## The full story

13 commits since v0.63.1, grouped by type and oldest first. Each entry is the commit message as written.

<details>
<summary>Features (2)</summary>

**feat(http): log the size of each model request** ([`3806ab4`](https://github.com/jjjermiah/opencode-plugboard/commit/3806ab479882f6a8445d4e63397a7041e7543390))

A request session showed about 14.5k cached prompt tokens for a 616-byte question, and nothing in plugboard said how big the request or its tool list was. The request log line now carries body_bytes, system_count, system_bytes, message_count, message_bytes, tool_count and tool_bytes.

What changed
- src/request-size.ts: the raw body is kept per request (readJsonBody remembers it), and the sizes are the UTF-8 size of the JSON of system, messages and tools as decoded, before the session remaps the tools. An empty part is 0 bytes, not the 2 bytes of "[]". A completions body with several prompts adds them up.
- Every model route (chat, completions, responses, messages, gemini) notes the body after reading it and the sizes once the request is decoded. The access line spreads them in. A request refused before it is decoded has none.
- Docs: configuration.md (Operating) and the monitoring guide.

Decisions
- The existing request line, not a new event: it already carries the app, model and id, so a size can be matched to a request. Counted per HTTP request, once, whatever the fan-out or the fallback chain does.
- Sizes come from the decoded PlugRequest, not each wire shape's own tool array, so the five front-ends share one definition. The wire wrappers (type: function, functionDeclarations) are not counted.
- request_tool_count and request_tool_bytes are not added to the usage record: the day record, its JSON reader, the sums and the report would all change, which is not a one-line change. Log only.

Validation
- bun run validate --mutations --skip examples,test: lint, typecheck, manifest, pack, docs and mutations pass (ten new P586 entries).
- bun test: 3886 pass, 0 fail. The validate test step still exits 1 on main as well: coverage 98.3% against a 98.9% floor, with the live suite skipped on this machine. Floors for test counts are raised.
- Live, isolated server, github-copilot/claude-haiku-5.5, a 336-byte chat body with one system message and one tool: the line printed body_bytes=336 system_bytes=18 message_bytes=63 tool_count=1 t
